chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Qasim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said:
A man wrote to al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him): "O my Master! Inform me of the best of this world and the Hereafter." So he wrote to him:
"In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. As for what follows:

Whoever seeks the pleasure of God despite the discontent of the people, God will suffice him in the affairs of the people. And whoever seeks the pleasure of the people despite the discontent of God, God will entrust him to the people. And peace."

key_terms.رضا الله: Pleasure of God — seeking divine approval in all actions
key_terms.سخط الناس: Discontent of the people — human disapproval when one follows God's commands
key_terms.وكله الله إلى الناس: God entrusts him to the people — left without divine aid

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Husayn say about seeking the pleasure of God versus the pleasure of people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (AS) wrote a letter in response to a man's question about the best of this world and the Hereafter. He taught that prioritizing God's pleasure over people's approval leads to divine protection, while the reverse leads to abandonment. This was guidance given in the early Islamic period when believers faced social pressure to compromise their principles.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
